old_problem: Procedure mixes Type 20 memory-device mapping fields with Type 3 chassis fields. Prior review treated field ownership as undecided. DeepSeek cannot prove effective intervals, Type 17 device handles, Type 19 array-range containment or interleave semantics from a heading grep.
disposition_reason: Resolve Pending and Source Conflict. DMTF assigns the mapping/interleave fields to Type 20, its Memory Device Handle to Type 17, and the mapped array range to Type 19; listed chassis fields are a mandatory Type 3 companion branch. Complete structure-aware topology validation preserves all source fields. Exact expected DIMM/range/interleave topology and Type 3 values are fail-closed Project Configuration; logs remain preserved.
decision_basis: XLSX row 1937, same-row tests.json/DeepSeek, GPT V2, historical record and ED-01 through ED-30 were read; the actual next queue row was directly opened as Functionality 1938 / Wistron-BIOS-00480-V002 / f7c1db6fe113b673.
DMTF field definitions determine Type 20 and Type 3 ownership, so both branches can be retained without an owner deciding which source fields to delete.
Each Type 20 Memory Device Handle must resolve to Type 17, its effective interval must fit the appropriate Type 19 array mapping, and legacy/extended address sentinel rules must be honored.
Partition Row Position, Interleave Position and Interleaved Data Depth are evaluated together against the approved platform interleave topology, not as isolated strings.
One approved warm reboot requires same-target Boot ID and OS Ready; complete raw and semantic evidence is repeated without clearing logs.
No dmidecode, SSH, reboot, log-clear, firmware, SMBIOS or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_name: SMBIOS Type 20 device-map, Type 17/19 relation, interleave and Type 3 persistence
test_case.purpose: Validate every Type 20 memory-device interval, Type 17 device handle, Type 19 array relationship and partition/interleave tuple plus every listed Type 3 chassis field against the exact recipe before and after reboot.
required_package: Exact target/BIOS/SMBIOS identity and versioned Type 20/17/19 topology: devices, effective ranges, handles, partition rows and interleave positions/depth
Validated dmidecode and complete Type 20/17/19/3 parser implementing legacy/extended sentinel and interval-containment rules
Secure access, approved OS warm reboot/window/Boot ID timeout and independent recovery
Preserved logs and protected memory-address/identity evidence policy
test_case.test_command: READ-ONLY COLLECTION AROUND ONE APPROVED REBOOT; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Capture target identity/logs and securely save complete `dmidecode --type 20`, referenced `--type 17`, containing `--type 19`, and `--type 3` output/status. Normalize every Type 20 effective interval; resolve its Type 17 device and Type 19 array, validate containment, partition row and interleave tuple against the recipe, and separately compare Type 3 fields. After one approved OS warm reboot with same-target Boot ID/OS Ready proof, repeat and semantic-diff all branches. No grep, log clear, insecure secrets, firmware/SMBIOS mutation or retry.
test_case.expected_result: Every expected Type 20 record has correct effective range, valid Type 17 device handle, valid containing Type 19 array map and correct partition/interleave tuple; intervals and address representation match the approved topology. All listed Type 3 fields are correct. Both branches remain semantically stable after OS Ready.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete successful pre/post Type 20/17/19/3 evidence, all handle/containment/sentinel/partition/interleave and chassis checks, exact identity, approved Boot ID-changing reboot and OS Ready. FAIL on missing/extra/malformed mapping, unresolved handle, range outside array, wrong interleave tuple, companion mismatch or reboot/health failure. NOT READY covers missing topology/oracles/access/recovery. Header-only output cannot PASS; end user owns verdict.
safety_gate: Read-only only; never change memory interleave, BIOS, SMBIOS, chassis security or firmware.
Preserve complete logs/output and protect address/identity values; never clear logs or suppress errors.
Use secure verified access and approved reboot/recovery; no plaintext secrets or disabled host verification.
Stop on wrong target, parser ambiguity, reboot failure or topology drift; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant, target/BIOS/SMBIOS/dmidecode/parser identities and Type 20/17/19 plus Type 3 matrices
Complete pre/post Type 20/17/19/3 raw output/status and hashes
Per-record effective interval, Type 17 handle, Type 19 containment, partition row and interleave evaluation
Approved reboot timeline, Boot IDs, same-target OS Ready and preserved platform logs/health
No-clear/no-write/no-retry audit, workload restore and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On reboot failure retain first evidence and follow only approved console/BMC recovery. On unresolved handle, invalid containment/interleave or topology drift, preserve full SMBIOS tables and firmware identity, make no BIOS/memory-setting change and escalate. Never auto-reboot or edit data to force alignment.
